name: MegaScale-Infer: Serving Mixture-of-Experts at Scale with Disaggregated Expert Parallelism
affiliations: School of Computer Science, Peking University, Beijing, China
problem: MoE's sparsity makes inference MEMORY-intensive rather than compute-intensive at decode, which drops GPU utilization and raises operating cost - and it means the attention and FFN halves of a layer want different parallelism strategies that a single monolithic layer layout cannot give them.
mechanism: DISAGGREGATES THE ATTENTION AND FFN MODULES WITHIN EACH LAYER, so the two are scaled independently with tailored parallelism strategies and can be deployed on HETEROGENEOUS hardware - the attention path is compute-bound and wants tensor parallelism, the FFN path is memory-bound and wants expert parallelism. The second mechanism is PING-PONG PIPELINE PARALLELISM: partition a request batch into MICRO-BATCHES and shuttle them between the attention side and the FFN side, which is what makes the disaggregation pay despite MoE sparsity - without a schedule that keeps both halves busy, splitting them just adds a hop. A high-performance M2N COMMUNICATION LIBRARY supports it, removing GPU-to-CPU data copies, group-initialization overhead and GPU synchronization that would otherwise dominate, and it exists specifically to minimize token-dispatch overhead across the disaggregation boundary.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim: up to 1.90x higher PER-GPU throughput than state-of-the-art solutions. The per-GPU qualifier is essential and must not be dropped: this is a utilization metric on disaggregated hardware, not an end-to-end request-latency number and not comparable to a single-node vLLM tok/s figure.

VENUE IS 'other' BECAUSE SIGCOMM IS NOT IN THE SCHEMA ENUM - the authoritative venue is SIGCOMM 2025, from the OpenReview note with venue 'SIGCOMM 2025' and venueid 'dblp.org/conf/SIGCOMM/2025'. The enum in schemas/paper.schema.json has no sigcomm entry, so the venue cannot be recorded honestly without either (a) claiming a venue the paper was not published at or (b) editing the schema, which is outside this pass's write scope. Recorded as 'other' with venue_track 'main' and the real venue in notes; the same convention the repo already uses for ColBERT and SPLADE. A future schema extension should add sigcomm. VERIFICATION CAVEAT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS NOT A CLEAN TITLE MATCH: the SIGCOMM note's title reads 'MegaScale-Infer: Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Model Serving with Disaggregated Expert Parallelism' - the PRE-PRINT title, not the current arXiv title. The identification therefore rests on the shared system name plus the identical mechanism (disaggregated expert parallelism) plus author-group overlap (Xin Jin appears on both the arXiv paper and the SIGCOMM record), not on a title string equality. This is the exact situation the repo's methodology rule anticipates, and it is recorded here rather than presented as a clean index hit. WHY IT IS A GAP: the repo's MoE serving work is DeepSpeed-MoE, MegaBlocks, Tutel/Flex, DeepSeek-V2/V3, Mixtral, OLMoE, MoEQuant, EAQuant and AlphaQ - all about MODELS or quantization. None disaggregates the layer internals for serving; the repo's disaggregation records are all prefill-vs-decode. Expert-vs-attention is a third axis and it is the one that matters when FFN weights dominate HBM traffic.
